Description: The 444NN port range (e.g., 44400, 44401) refers to SAP Message Server (MsgServer) interfaces exposed over HTTPS. These are the encrypted variants of the 81NN HTTP-based ports, offering the same routing and landscape coordination features with TLS encryption for secure communication.
Deployment Context: Message Server handles central communication coordination in SAP NetWeaver-based systems, particularly in multi-instance or load-balanced setups. The HTTPS variant is commonly found in hardened landscapes or in scenarios where internal service discovery must comply with secure transport requirements (e.g., regulatory or cloud-enforced security policies).
Functional Capabilities: The MsgServer HTTPS interface exposes key metadata for routing users and services. It reveals logon groups, available instances, roles of each application server (dialog, update, etc.), and dynamic priorities. These endpoints are leveraged by SAP Web Dispatcher, sapgui.exe, and other SAP clients to determine which backend server should handle a request.
Authentication Mechanisms: The 444NN ports may or may not enforce client-side authentication, depending on configuration. By default, they do not require credentials for basic routing info — making this interface useful but potentially sensitive. If client certificates are enforced, they may be tied into X.509 trust chains or internal PKI systems.
Stack Characteristics: Message Server interfaces are typically bound to the Central Services Instance (SCS/ASCS). On ABAP systems, this enables SAP GUI or Web Dispatcher to retrieve updated logon group assignments. On Java stacks, it facilitates HTTP load balancing. MsgServer operates alongside the ICM but functions primarily as a routing authority.
Assessment Goals: The 444NN module will eventually identify logon groups, system roles, load balancing metrics, and multi-instance presence. It will extract endpoint data from `/msgserver/html/group` and `/msgserver/text/logon`, validate TLS certificate details, and help visualize backend topology.
Security Implications: Unprotected MsgServer interfaces leak landscape intelligence. Attackers can use exposed logon groups to identify available backend hosts, SID and hostname mappings, and routing preferences — useful for lateral movement or DoS attacks. Improperly configured MsgServer may even allow control or spoofing of group behavior.
Assessment Notes: An open 444NN port indicates that this SAP system is set up for secure service discovery. If Web Dispatcher or GUI clients fetch metadata from here, the MsgServer plays a critical role in user distribution logic. This is a key discovery and mapping point in complex or distributed SAP landscapes.
